title: Water Management in Rice Cultivation
title_hi: धान की खेती में जल प्रबंधन
content:
Proper water management is the single most important factor for healthy rice. Poor water management increases disease risk, reduces nutrient uptake, and wastes water.

Key principles:
1. Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD): Instead of continuous flooding, allow the field to dry until the water table drops 15 cm below surface, then re-flood. This saves 30% water and reduces methane emissions without yield loss.
2. Drainage before harvest: Drain the field 7-10 days before harvest. This hardens the grain, reduces lodging, and makes mechanical harvesting easier.
3. Waterlogging damage: Standing water for >3 days during vegetative stage causes root rot and nutrient deficiency. Emergency drainage trenches may be needed.
4. Seedling stage: Maintain 2-3 cm water depth during the first week after transplanting for better establishment.

Signs of water stress:
- Leaves rolling inward (drought)
- Yellowing of lower leaves (waterlogging)
- Reduced tillering
- Stunted growth
content_hi:
धान की खेती में उचित जल प्रबंधन सबसे महत्वपूर्ण है।

मुख्य सिद्धांत:
1. AWD विधि — बारी-बारी से सुखाना और पानी भरना।
2. कटाई से 7-10 दिन पहले पानी निकाल दें।
3. जलभराव से जड़ सड़न।
4. रोपाई के बाद 2-3 सेमी पानी।
summary: Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) saves 30% water. Drain 7-10 days before harvest. Avoid waterlogging for >3 days.
summary_hi: AWD विधि से 30% पानी बचता है। कटाई से 7-10 दिन पहले खेत सुखाएं। 3 दिन से अधिक जलभराव न होने दें।
actions: Adopt Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD): irrigate only when water table drops 15 cm below surface — use a simple PVC pipe to monitor.
If continuous rain has waterlogged the field for 3+ days, dig emergency drainage channels to the lowest edge of the field.
At grain-filling stage, maintain 2-3 cm standing water until 7-10 days before harvest, then drain completely.
Check for leaf rolling in the morning — if leaves are rolled before 9 AM, the crop is water-stressed and needs irrigation.
warnings: Do NOT keep the field continuously flooded throughout the season — this wastes water, increases disease, and produces methane.
Sudden drainage during flowering can cause sterility — transition slowly over 3-4 days.
